term: first-order justification and the global knowledge/justification norm
definition: KnowledgeRequiresJustification F p justified says for every model world w, Knows F p w implies justified w for the fixed proposition p. The supplied justified predicate records justification of p, not knowledge that p is justified. Knows F justified w is the latter higher-order condition. No path, truth predicate or certainty predicate defines justification.
note: The norm is explicit and global because the transfer applies it at epistemic alternatives. Actual justification and truth of this norm remain unestablished. Different first-order theories could supply the predicate; the proof does not select one.
